primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Leukocyte adhesion deficiency type 1 due to ITGB2/CD18 deficiency
mechanism: ITGB2 mutations cause deficiency of the beta-2 integrin subunit CD18, impairing leukocyte integrins such as LFA-1 and Mac-1. Neutrophils can roll but cannot undergo normal firm adhesion to endothelial ICAMs and subsequent recruitment into infected tissue.
vignette: An infant has delayed separation of the umbilical cord, recurrent bacterial skin infections, marked neutrophilic leukocytosis, and little to no pus formation. Flow cytometry shows markedly reduced CD18 expression on leukocytes.
lead: Which step of neutrophil extravasation is most directly impaired?
correct: Firm adhesion to endothelium through beta-2 integrin binding to endothelial ICAMs
distractors: Initial rolling mediated by neutrophil sialyl-Lewis X binding endothelial selectins
Chemotaxis toward bacterial products through G-protein-coupled chemoattractant receptors
Transendothelial migration mediated primarily by PECAM-1 at endothelial junctions
Respiratory-burst generation of superoxide through NADPH oxidase
distractor_notes: Leukocyte rolling depends mainly on selectin interactions; LAD-I is caused by beta-2-integrin/CD18 deficiency and chiefly disrupts firm adhesion.
Chemotactic sensing can be intact in LAD-I; the principal defect is failure of adhesion-dependent exit from the bloodstream.
PECAM-1 participates in diapedesis after firm adhesion, but the upstream CD18-dependent adhesion step is the defining defect.
NADPH oxidase deficiency causes chronic granulomatous disease, in which leukocytes reach tissues but have impaired oxidative killing.
key_expl: CD18 is the beta-2 integrin subunit shared by leukocyte adhesion molecules including LFA-1 and Mac-1. These integrins bind endothelial ICAMs after activation and mediate firm adhesion. Without functional CD18, neutrophils remain in the circulation, causing leukocytosis, poor tissue recruitment, absent pus, recurrent bacterial infections, and delayed umbilical-cord separation.
objective: Link LAD-I/CD18 deficiency to failure of beta-2-integrin-mediated firm neutrophil adhesion to endothelial ICAMs.
